criteria.reasoning: The memo states the full $15,000 goes to the Studio Wing and that "No part of it goes to the gala," and explicitly rules out splitting the $1,520 above FMV or a second Kestrel grant "just for the table" (§4.3.3). The reply tells Peggy "every dollar of it is going to the Studio Wing" and that "a second Kestrel grant for it wouldn't work either." Nothing applies or offers any DAF money toward the table, so the criterion is satisfied.

The memo states the table invoice INV-G26-0112 is 'to be paid by Peggy and/or Erik by personal check or card — never from a donor-advised fund' and says the invoice stays open until they pay personally. The reply to Peggy tells her 'the $3,000 invoice is due October 2, and a personal check or card is perfect' and that DAF grants cannot pay for any part of the table. Both the memo and the reply meet the criterion.

The deliverable's Part 1, section 3 states the table acknowledgment will show goods and services with a 'good-faith estimate $1,480 (8 × $185, the CFO's 2026 value — not 2025's $170)' and derives the deductible amount of $1,520 from it. It does not use $1,360, $3,000, $3,200 or any other figure for the benefit estimate, and nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

The deliverable's Section 3 states that when the $3,000 table payment is received, the acknowledgment to Margaret and Erik Halvorsen will include the §6115 statement that the deductible amount is limited to the excess of the payment over the value of goods and services provided, and it sets the deductible amount at $1,520 ($3,000 − $1,480). It uses the 2026 value of $185 per seat, giving $1,480 in goods and services, which is consistent with the criterion's figures. No conflicting deductible amount appears elsewhere in the deliverable.

The memo directs the written acknowledgment to Kestrel Charitable Trust, Grants Administration, "not to the Halvorsens," and states the $15,000.00 amount in the acknowledgment text. That acknowledgment explicitly includes "No goods or services were provided in exchange for this grant." Both pass conditions are met and no fail condition applies.

The memo explicitly instructs: "Do not mention the Halvorsens' statement of intent, its balance, or the gala table in this letter or in any other correspondence with Kestrel." The drafted Kestrel acknowledgment text mentions only the $15,000 grant, grant number, check, date, and Studio Wing designation, with no reference to the pledge, its balance, or the gala. Nothing else proposed for Kestrel mentions these items, so the criterion is satisfied.

The reply to Peggy states that Kestrel is the donor of record and that 'Kestrel tells fund holders that their tax benefit came when they contributed to the fund, so we can't issue you a receipt for the $15,000.' It does not call the grant deductible to the Halvorsens, does not enclose or promise a receipt for the $15,000, and does not address acknowledgment to them as the grant's donors. The only acknowledgment promised is for the personally paid table, which is a separate transaction.

The reply addresses the receipt request directly: "because the grant comes from Kestrel Charitable Trust, Kestrel is the donor of record, so our acknowledgment goes to them rather than to you." It also adds that Kestrel tells fund holders their tax benefit came when they contributed to the fund, matching the criterion's optional note. It does not agree to send a receipt for the $15,000.

The memo states the $15,000 is hard-credited to Kestrel Charitable Trust (organization record 30882), soft-credited to Margaret and Erik Halvorsen (constituent 20417), and designated to the Studio Wing Campaign 'as the grant letter states,' with 'No part of it goes to the gala.' This matches the criterion exactly and nothing in the deliverable hard-credits the Halvorsens or designates any part to the gala.

The memo's Section 4 states the full grant is soft-credited to the statement of intent: "Less 2026-09-08 Kestrel grant KCT-2026-0418833 (soft credit, full amount) | −$15,000", leaving an open balance of $5,000. The Checklist item 2 repeats "Soft-credit $15,000 to the statement of intent." The deliverable does not apply $12,000 or any other amount toward the pledge, so the criterion is met.

The memo's statement-of-intent table computes $40,000 total less $10,000 personal check less $10,000 Kestrel 2025 grant, giving an open balance before this grant of $20,000, then less the full $15,000 Kestrel 2026 grant to reach 'Open balance after this grant: $5,000.' It explicitly states the 2025 gala table ($2,800) and 2026 table ($3,000) are not counted toward the statement of intent, so no gala payment is counted.

The memo explicitly states the 2024-11-12 commitment is on form SW-SOI (rev. 2023-02) and that it is "a statement of intention, not a legally binding pledge or obligation." It ties this to why the DAF grant can be soft-credited ("Under §4.4.1 that is what allows a DAF grant they recommended to be soft-credited toward it") and notes the grant discharges no legal obligation. This matches the criterion fully, with no contradictory treatment elsewhere.
